name: wordpress-docker
title: Çınar Mimarlık — WordPress studio site
description: Stock WordPress 6 (official images) with a bind-mounted custom theme and mu-plugin providing a 'project' custom post type; provisioned idempotently by setup.sh via a wp-cli sidecar.

env.name: WP_HOME
env.description: Public site URL; change to the deployed domain

env.name: WP_SITEURL
env.description: WordPress core URL; same as WP_HOME

env.name: WORDPRESS_CONFIG_EXTRA
env.description: PHP appended to wp-config.php; keep the default

env.name: WP_ADMIN_USER
env.description: Admin user created by setup.sh on first install

env.name: WP_ADMIN_PASSWORD
env.description: Admin password created by setup.sh on first install

env.name: WP_ADMIN_EMAIL
env.description: Admin e-mail created by setup.sh on first install

auth.description: WordPress native login (/wp-login.php) with auth cookies; /wp-admin/ redirects anonymous users to the login form. Public site and REST read endpoints need no auth.

persistence: Named volumes: db_data (MariaDB), wp_core (/var/www/html incl. wp-config.php), wp_content (uploads/plugins). Theme and mu-plugin are bind-mounted from the repo. Content is created by setup.sh into the database.
notes: Docker-only. After `docker compose up -d` you MUST run ./setup.sh once (idempotent, ~1-2 min) – it waits for MariaDB, runs `wp core install`, activates the theme and seeds pages/projects/menu via the wpcli sidecar (compose profile 'cli', never started by `up`). Until then the health route redirects to the install wizard. To serve from another domain set WP_HOME and WP_SITEURL in .env before running setup.sh (or afterwards – constants override DB values). Only port 8008 is published; MariaDB is internal. XML-RPC is disabled. The wpcli service runs as uid 33 to match the Apache image.
